postTitle: Account Consolidation: Cleaning Up Financial Sprawl
topic: Forgotten accounts are not free; they leak money every year

assumptions.notes: Jiri, 38 (same character as post 44: €45,000 in investments and a pension). 13 accounts at 7 institutions. Dormant fees: 3 accounts × €5 a month × 12 = €180 a year. Old pension €30,000 at 0.75% fund fees against 0.05% in his current plan: 0.70% × €30,000 = €210 a year. Idle cash €6,000 in two old savings accounts at about 0%, against an illustrative 3% elsewhere: €180 a year. Total €570 a year; ten years €5,700 before any growth. Same method as the blog post (€5 dormant fees, 0.75% against 0.05%, idle cash against a better rate); amounts scaled to Jiri. Illustrative.

hookVariants.narration: Your forgotten accounts are still doing something. Mostly, costing you.
Count your financial accounts. Most people get the number wrong, and pay for it.

beats.narration: Jiri has thirteen accounts at seven institutions. Three he never uses charge five euros a month each. That is a hundred and eighty a year.
A pension from a job he left charges point seven five percent. His current plan charges point zero five. On thirty thousand euros, the gap is two hundred and ten a year.
And six thousand euros sits in old savings accounts earning almost nothing. At an illustrative three percent elsewhere, that is another hundred and eighty.
About five hundred and seventy euros a year. For nothing.
It never arrives as one bill. That is why it lasts for years.
The fix is a weekend. List every account. Give each one a label. Move or close the ones with no clear job. Then keep things to a few institutions.

caption.instagram:
Your forgotten accounts are still doing something. Mostly, costing you.

Jiri, 38, has 13 accounts at 7 institutions. Three dormant ones charge €5 a month each: €180 a year. An old pension charges 0.75% where his current plan charges 0.05%: €210 a year on €30,000. And €6,000 sits in old savings accounts at almost nothing, missing about €180 a year at an illustrative 3%. About €570 a year, for nothing.

The four step clean up: list every account, label each one essential, optimising or dormant, move or close the ones with no clear job, then keep things to a few institutions.
